question: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CaO**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CaO** has the **highest boiling point** among the given options.
 
• Boiling points are influenced by the strength of the ionic bonds in the compound.
 
• CaO has a** very high lattice energy due** to the **strong ionic bond between Ca²⁺ and O²⁻**.
 
• In comparison, NaCl, LiCl, and CaCl₂ have lower boiling points because their ionic bonds are not as strong as in CaO.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lattice energy** is a measure of the** strength of the forces between the ions in an ionic solid**.
 
• Higher lattice energy generally results in higher boiling points.
 
• CaO, being an oxide, has a stronger ionic bond compared to chlorides due to the higher charge of O²⁻ compared to Cl⁻.
 
• The melting and boiling points of ionic compounds are generally high due to the strong electrostatic forces between the ions.
